messages:
jessica_support: Hey, incoming from a customer (acct: acme-inc) — their JSON parser started failing intermittently this morning after a traffic spike. They say the API returns valid JSON usually, but sometimes the 'answer' field contains HTML comments/tags and the client JSON parser chokes. Full customer error: "JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)".

mike_eng: Can you paste an example of the exact body they receive? Is it a 200 with malformed JSON or a non-JSON content-type?

jessica_support: Pasted payload from their logs (sanitized):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "id": "resp-123",
  "model": "redwood-13b-v1",
  "output": {
    "answer": "<!-- debug: fallback model: redwood-13b-quant -->
<div class=\"snippet\">Here is the summary...<\/div>",
    "tokens": 72
  }
}
```

jessica_support: Notice the HTML comment at the start of the string and a small HTML snippet. Customer's strict parser uses a JSON schema that expects 'answer' to be plain text without markup and fails downstream.

sam_eng-runtime: This screams like smart-routing fallback. Our routing logs show a fallback to a quantized variant when capacity was low. Quantized variants sometimes return small debugging annotations in text-mode outputs if their decoder has different system-message handling. I'll pull the routing trace.

monitor-bot: [routing] 2026-03-17T09:18:06Z request_id=req-9802 routed to redwood-13b-v1 -> capacity low -> fallback redwood-13b-quant-v2 (zone us-east1)

mike_eng: Thanks. Can you repro locally by forcing the fallback? If we can reproduce we can add a post-processing step to strip HTML comments for structured endpoints.

sam_eng-runtime: Repro steps I ran:
1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "X-Client-Mode: structured-json" -d '{"model":"redwood-13b-v1","prompt":"<TASK>summarize</TASK>","max_tokens":80}'
2) Simulate capacity by setting ROUTING_OVERRIDE=model=redwood-13b-quant-v2 on the request (internal header).
3) Response returned with embedded comment. Example: 
```
{
  "id":"resp-local-1",
  "model":"redwood-13b-quant-v2",
  "output":{"answer":"<!-- fallback-quant note: trimmed kv -->Summary text...","tokens":64}
}
```

sam_eng-runtime: So confirmed. The quantized variant prepends HTML-style comment used by a downstream LM-internal debug layer. It's valid JSON but breaks consumer schema because they forbid markup.

olivia_sre: We should treat structured-json routes as strict schema endpoints. Two quick mitigations: 1) Proxy-level sanitizer to strip HTML tags/comments from string fields for structured endpoints, 2) Prevent fallback to variants that annotate outputs for any request that sets X-Client-Mode: structured-json (or similar). Both are feasible short-term.

mike_eng: Long-term we should add variant capability flags in the model catalog (e.g., allowed_for_structured=true/false). Then routing can check capabilities before fallback. Also add a warning in the model metadata when a variant is known to inject annotations.

jessica_support: Customer is requesting a timeline. They said this broke their nightly ingest job and they had to rollback. They're asking if we can pin their traffic to the non-quant model or add a quick filter.

sam_eng-runtime: For immediate relief I can push a routing-policy override for acme-inc so their requests avoid quantized variants for 24h. But this needs approval from infra on capacity.

olivia_sre: Approved as emergency SOP. I'll apply a temporary tenant-level routing rule: pin model family redwood-13b to non-quant variants for customer acme-inc. Also adding a proxy sanitize rule for Content-Type: application/json requests that have X-Client-Mode: structured-json — it will strip leading HTML comments and basic tags from string outputs.

jessica_support: Thank you. Customer wants a quick repro test from our side then we'll ask them to re-run their job.

sam_eng-runtime: Done — I confirmed pinned rule is live. Repro after pin returns clean JSON:
```
{
  "id":"resp-pinned-1",
  "model":"redwood-13b-v1",
  "output":{"answer":"Summary text...","tokens":70}
}
```

mike_eng: Follow-ups:
- Add model capability flag in catalog (eng + infra)
- Update smart routing to honor capability flags for structured endpoints (eng-runtime)
- Add unit/regression test to ensure fallback never injects markup for structured-json API (qa/eng)
- Document in Support KB that structured endpoints may be pinned to avoid quantized fallbacks.

jessica_support: I'll communicate timeline to customer: immediate pin + sanitize rule applied; ETA for permanent fix: 2 weeks (catalog flags + routing checks).

olivia_sre: I'll open an incident ticket to track this (INC-2026-134). Assigning to sam and mike.

mike_eng: Also let's log any billing/latency impacts. Quantized variants were cheaper; pinning will increase unit cost for that tenant until a safer quantized variant is certified. Finance should notify customer separately if usage changes.

jessica_support: Noted; looping in billing if they ask.

sam_eng-runtime: I'll start a small sweep to find other structured endpoints that have fallback-enabled variants that annotate outputs. Will post results here.

jessica_support: Thanks everyone. I'll update acme-inc and close when customer confirms. :thumbsup:
